A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 23-page CC-ICL study, including Appendices A–C. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that pages 2–23 are identical; differences are confined to the first page.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original CC-Bench evaluations, multi-criterion training experiments, ablations, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the original CC-Bench evaluations, multi-criterion training experiments, ablations, and case studies.

M1.justification: The CC-ICL procedure and Multi-Criterion Training strategy are unchanged. Both versions train on the same query paired with support sets whose criterion-sensitive labels differ.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Industrial Inspection, Medical Diagnosis, and Video Surveillance coverage, alongside MMBench and MMStar. Dataset categories and two- and three-criterion scenarios are unchanged, including the appendices.

E2.justification: The seven base VLMs in Table 1, Base/MCT comparisons in Table 2, prompt-modality comparisons, and single-criterion training controls in Table 13 are identical.

E3.justification: The data splits, support-set pairing, CI/CS metrics, temperature-zero inference, default three-shot evaluation, and training settings remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B. Supplementary evaluation protocols are also identical.

E4.justification: Sections 5.4–5.5 and Appendix C retain the same reasoning analysis, cross-domain and criterion-count transfer studies, shot-count and prompt-modality ablations, training-composition analysis, response distributions, and case studies.

E5.justification: Table 8 reports random seed 42 in both versions. Neither version adds repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical, including Tables 1–4 and 10–13 and the appendix plots and cases. For example, Table 2 retains Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct MCT sensitivity scores of 68.32% for Industrial Inspection and 83.11% for Medical Diagnosis.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same task and criterion definitions, probabilistic formulations in Equations 1–3, and Criterion Invariance and Criterion Sensitivity definitions in Equations 4–5. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning CC-ICL, CC-Bench, rigid boundary bias, and MCT's effectiveness. The added code-access sentence does not change these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of rigid boundary bias, context-conditioned reasoning, robustness tradeoffs, and generalization are unchanged. The qualifications concerning limited transfer from static-image domains to video also remain identical.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and the Megvii-Algo-Team/CC-ICL GitHub repository address to the abstract; v1 provides neither. Existing implementation details are unchanged. This establishes added access information, not verification of the repository's contents or availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning of criterion adaptation relative to prior ICL research are unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 expands the author name 'J. Wang' to 'Jikai Wang', appends the code-access sentence to the abstract, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining wording and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: The first page has a small layout adjustment accommodating the code statement and longer author name. All figures, tables, and page layouts from page 2 through the appendices render identically.

improvement.justification: The added repository address gives readers an implementation access point absent from v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and appendices are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish whether the repository is accessible or complete.
